description: Defines dietary and health goals that coaches can set for clients, with nutritional targets, compatible recipe dimension thresholds, and coaching strategies.

weight_loss.label: Weight Loss
weight_loss.description: Reduce caloric intake while maintaining satiety and nutritional adequacy. Emphasizes low-calorie, high-volume, high-satiety meals.

health.rationale: Must be nutritionally dense to avoid hunger on reduced calories

satiety.rationale: High satiety prevents overeating between meals

time_to_cook.rationale: Complex recipes raise dropout risk for calorie-restricted clients

technicality.rationale: Sustainability drops if cooking feels like a chore

cleanup_difficulty.rationale: High cleanup friction discourages consistent home cooking

weight_loss.coaching_strategy: Prioritize high-satiety, low-health-score (meaning healthy) recipes. Batch-cook proteins and vegetables. Suggest swaps that increase volume without calories (extra vegetables, broth-based soups).

muscle_gain.label: Muscle Gain
muscle_gain.description: Support muscle hypertrophy with adequate protein, caloric surplus, and nutrient timing around workouts.

health.rationale: Need quality nutrients but higher calories are acceptable

satiety.rationale: Moderate satiety helps meet higher caloric needs without excessive fullness

time_to_cook.rationale: Athletes often cook larger portions; moderate complexity is acceptable

technicality.rationale: Can handle moderate technique but efficiency matters

output_yield.rationale: Need recipes that produce multiple servings for meal prep

muscle_gain.coaching_strategy: Focus on protein-dense recipes with good output yield. Encourage batch cooking of grains and proteins. Suggest simple sauces and marinades to add calories without complexity.

heart_health.label: Heart Health
heart_health.description: Reduce sodium, saturated fat, and refined carbohydrates. Emphasize omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and antioxidant-rich ingredients.

health.rationale: Heart-healthy recipes must score very well on nutritional quality

satiety.rationale: Satiety prevents overconsumption of processed snacks

ingredients.rationale: Should use accessible whole food ingredients, not exotic items

reproducibility.rationale: Clients need to reliably reproduce heart-healthy meals

time_to_cook.rationale: Sustainable heart-healthy cooking requires approachable recipes

heart_health.coaching_strategy: Emphasize recipes rich in omega-3s (salmon, sardines), fiber (legumes, whole grains), and low sodium. Suggest salt-free seasoning blends. Prioritize baking, steaming, and poaching over frying.

diabetes_management.label: Diabetes Management
diabetes_management.description: Stabilize blood sugar through low-glycemic meals with controlled carbohydrate portions and consistent meal timing.

health.rationale: Nutritional quality is paramount for blood sugar management

satiety.rationale: Stable satiety prevents blood sugar crashes and binge eating

reproducibility.rationale: Consistent carbohydrate amounts require precise recipes

dimension_constraints.sugar_profile_note: All recipes should score 1-3 on health.sugar_profile

diabetes_management.coaching_strategy: Build meal plans around low-glycemic index ingredients. Pair carbs with protein and fat to slow absorption. Emphasize consistent portion sizes and meal timing. Avoid recipes with high sugar_profile scores.

anti_inflammatory.label: Anti-Inflammatory
anti_inflammatory.description: Reduce systemic inflammation through antioxidant-rich, omega-3-heavy, and minimally processed meals.

health.rationale: Anti-inflammatory diets require maximum nutrient density

ingredients.rationale: May tolerate specialty sourcing for turmeric, wild salmon, etc.

cooking_steps.rationale: Gentle cooking methods (steaming, low-heat sauteing) are preferred; avoid charring

technicality.rationale: Should be approachable for chronic inflammation clients who may have low energy

anti_inflammatory.coaching_strategy: Focus on colorful vegetables, fatty fish, nuts, seeds, and anti-inflammatory spices (turmeric, ginger, garlic). Prioritize steaming, poaching, and raw preparations. Avoid high-heat methods and processed oils.

endurance_fueling.label: Endurance Fueling
endurance_fueling.description: Provide sustained energy for endurance athletes through strategic carbohydrate loading and nutrient timing.

health.rationale: Need carb-heavy meals; some refined carbs acceptable during training windows

satiety.rationale: Moderate satiety allows consuming enough calories without excessive fullness

output_yield.rationale: Need substantial portion sizes for caloric needs

endurance_fueling.coaching_strategy: Time carb-heavy meals around training. Prioritize simple recipes with high output yield. Batch-cook grains and starches. Suggest easy-to-digest pre-workout and simple recovery meals.

gut_health.label: Gut Health
gut_health.description: Support digestive health through prebiotic fibers, probiotic foods, and minimally processed, easily digestible meals.

health.rationale: Gut-healing diets require high nutrient density and minimal processing

ingredients.rationale: Should use whole, recognizable ingredients; minimal processed items

technicality.rationale: Clients with gut issues often have low energy; keep cooking simple

gut_health.coaching_strategy: Emphasize fermented foods (kimchi, yogurt, sauerkraut), prebiotic fibers (garlic, onions, asparagus), and bone broth. Recommend simple cooking methods. Suggest food journaling to identify triggers.

stress_reduction.label: Stress Reduction
stress_reduction.description: Minimize cooking-related stress by recommending simple, low-complexity recipes. Nutritional choices that support cortisol management (magnesium, B vitamins, complex carbs).

technicality.rationale: Primary goal is reducing cooking stress; must be easy

cleanup_difficulty.rationale: Low cleanup keeps the experience pleasant

reproducibility.rationale: Recipes should be easy to get right even when distracted

stress_reduction.coaching_strategy: Start with one-pan and sheet-pan meals. Prioritize recipes with fewer than 6 ingredients. Suggest meal kits or pre-prepped vegetables for highest-stress periods. Build confidence with reliable, high-reproducibility recipes.

budget_optimization.label: Budget Optimization
budget_optimization.description: Maximize nutritional value per dollar spent. Emphasize affordable proteins, seasonal vegetables, and minimal food waste.

health.rationale: Budget meals should still be nutritious

output_yield.rationale: Higher yield means lower cost per serving

satiety.rationale: High-satiety budget meals prevent expensive snacking

dimension_constraints.waste_ratio_note: Prefer recipes with low waste_ratio (output_yield.waste_ratio score 1-3)

ingredients.rationale: Should use affordable, commonly available ingredients

dimension_constraints.leftover_quality_note: Prefer recipes where leftover_quality score is 1-4 (holds well as leftovers)

budget_optimization.coaching_strategy: Focus on beans, lentils, eggs, chicken thighs, and seasonal produce. Plan weekly menus around sales. Batch-cook staple grains and legumes. Use root-to-leaf cooking to minimize waste. Prefer recipes that freeze well.

family_meal_planning.label: Family Meal Planning
family_meal_planning.description: Produce balanced meals that satisfy diverse family members including children. Emphasizes scalability, mild flavors, and adaptable recipes.

health.rationale: Balanced nutrition for growing children and adults

satiety.rationale: Meals must fill everyone up to reduce snacking

time_to_cook.rationale: Busy families need reasonably timed meals

sections.rationale: Separate components allow customization for picky eaters (sauce on the side, etc.)

family_meal_planning.coaching_strategy: Choose recipes that scale well and allow deconstruction (separate proteins, sauces, sides). Use mild base flavors with optional spice additions. Prepare extra portions for lunch leftovers. Involve children in simple tasks to build food acceptance.

general_wellness.label: General Wellness
general_wellness.description: Balanced approach to everyday healthy eating without strict dietary restrictions. Focus on whole foods, variety, and sustainable habits.

health.rationale: Should lean healthy without being restrictive

satiety.rationale: Satisfying meals prevent overeating and snacking

time_to_cook.rationale: Sustainable long-term cooking habits require reasonable time

reproducibility.rationale: Recipes should work reliably to build trust in home cooking

general_wellness.coaching_strategy: Rotate through protein sources, grain types, and vegetables for variety. Build a repertoire of 10-15 reliable recipes. Gradually introduce new techniques as confidence builds. Focus on the 80/20 rule: 80% whole foods, 20% flexibility.

sleep_optimization.label: Sleep Optimization
sleep_optimization.description: Evening meals designed to support quality sleep through tryptophan-rich proteins, complex carbs, and minimal stimulation (low spice, low sugar, moderate portions).

health.rationale: Sleep-supportive meals should be nutritionally clean

satiety.rationale: Satisfied but not overfull; heavy meals disrupt sleep

time_to_cook.rationale: Evening cooking should be relaxing, not stressful

technicality.rationale: End-of-day cooking should be simple and calming

dimension_constraints.sugar_profile_note: All recipes should score 1-3 on health.sugar_profile (no sugar crashes before bed)

sleep_optimization.coaching_strategy: Recommend turkey, salmon, eggs, nuts, and seeds for tryptophan. Pair with complex carbs (sweet potatoes, whole grains) to aid serotonin production. Avoid caffeine, high sugar, heavy spice, and large portions. Suggest eating 2-3 hours before bed.
